author: BBC News
description:
Five European countries say the Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny was killed using a deadly toxin found in poison dart frogs in South America.
 
France, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden and the United Kingdom say traces of epibatidine were found in samples from Navalny's body and "highly likely" resulted in his death in a Siberian penal colony two years ago. It says only the Russian government had the "means, motive and opportunity" to use this poison - which is apparently 200 times stronger than morphine.
 
The Kremlin dismissed the finding as "an information campaign" and has rejected accusations that it was responsible for the death of the fierce Putin critic.
 
The BBC's world news correspondent Joe Inwood takes us through what we know about the opposition leader's death, and what the toxin report reveals about Russia's access to and use of rare poisons.
 
New episodes of the Global News Podcast are published twice a day. You can listen here: https://link.mgln.ai/GNP-YT

title: Was Alexei Navalny killed by a dart frog toxin? | Global News Podcast

author: BBC News
description:
The UK government is considering accelerating planned increases to defence spending.

The news comes after the PM dropped some heavy hints that he was ready to spend more on defence during his speech at the Munich Security Conference on Saturday.

Katya Adler and James Landale drop by to explain how America is trying to rewrite the global order… and get Europe to sign on and Joe Pike explains why spending more on defence is never politically straightforward.

Plus, Joe and Adam discuss the government’s decision to scrap it’s plans to postpone elections for 30 councils after recieving “legal advice”. They also review the government’s latest proposals to crack down on online safety for children and Starmer’s response to claims that a Labour Think Tank paid a private investigator to look into journalists.

You can now listen to Newscast on a smart speaker. If you want to listen, just say "Ask BBC Sounds to play Newscast”. It works on most smart speakers.

You can join our Newscast online
title: Is Europe ready for Donald Trump's vision for the world? | BBC Newscast

author: BBC News
description:
Iron Lung is YouTuber Markiplier’s debut sci‑fi horror film, based on the hit indie game where a convict explores an ocean made entirely of human blood - alone. The movie debuted with a $17.8M opening weekend, climbing past $43M worldwide. 
 
Markiplier wrote, directed, financed, and starred in the film, and he’s been open about the production’s wildest challenge: using more fake blood than any movie before it. As a result, real‑world blood donation drives took place across the US, with fans lining up outside cinemas to give blood after screenings.
 
Markiplier worked closely with game creator David Szymanski to keep the world authentic, relying heavily on physical effects. He spoke to Newsbeat's Naomi de Souza about the film and its challenges.

author: BBC News
description:
UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer is considering making a significant increase in defence spending, the BBC has learned.
 
Last year Starmer promised to spend 2.5% of national economic output – measured as gross domestic product (GDP) - on core defence by April 2027.
 
Now, Downing Street is mulling over the idea of meeting the existing spending target earlier than planned at a potential cost of billions of pounds.
 
The PM signalled his attitude over the weekend at the Munich Security Conference, telling world leaders: "To meet the wider threat, it's clear that we are going to have to spend more, faster."

author: BBC News
description:
US and Iranian officials are preparing to hold a second round of talks on Tuesday in Switzerland, but US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said the discussions are “likely to be complicated”.
 
This follows Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu saying the US must require Iran to relinquish all of its enriched uranium and be barred from enriching more, as part of any nuclear deal with Tehran.
 
In a speech in Jerusalem on Sunday, Netanyahu outlined several conditions he wanted, including that "all enriched material has to leave Iran" and that "there should be no enrichment capability".

author: BBC News
description:
A former energy minister in Ukraine has been detained while attempting to leave the country, authorities have said.
 
German Galushchenko, who was forced out of his government role last year after being among officials named in a corruption scandal, was reportedly apprehended while on a train leaving Ukraine. It is unclear where he intended to travel to.
 
He was one of several government figures implicated in an alleged $100m (£75m) embezzlement scheme in November.
 
The National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (Nabu) said in a statement on Sunday that its detectives had detained the former energy minister "while crossing the state border".

description:
Savannah Guthrie has issued a plea for her 84-year-old mother's release two weeks after she disappeared, urging anyone involved that "it is never too late to do the right thing".
 
In the US TV anchor's latest video appeal, she addresses "whoever has her, or knows where she is", adding that Nancy Guthrie's loved ones "still have hope".
 
It comes as investigators analyse DNA found on a glove that they recovered. The glove being studied appears to match one that was worn by a suspect who appeared in doorbell-camera footage taken the night Nancy Guthrie went missing.

author: BBC News
description:
Two years to the day since the death of Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny in a Siberian prison, floral tributes have been left in Moscow by supporters.
 
The UK and allies have blamed the Kremlin following analysis of material samples found on his body, which shows he was killed using a poison developed from a dart frog toxin.
 
According to Tass news agency, Moscow has dismissed the finding as "an information campaign", but UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper said there is no explanation for the toxin, called epibatidine, being found.

author: BBC News
description:
UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer has pledged to respond more quickly to close loopholes in laws designed to protect children online.
 
Under new proposals, Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots would be included in the Online Safety Act.
 
"Technology is moving really fast, and the law has got to keep up," Sir Keir said, adding that he wanted Britain to be a leader in online safety.
 
Other new elements proposed include a measure to require tech giants to preserve all of the data on a child's phone if they die.
 
But opponents have accused the government of "inaction", and have called for Parliament to be given a vote on the social media ban for children.
